title: Aviation Life Support Systems Training and Acquisition Manager
raw_text:
Job Title                                                                                                                         Job Code
Aviation Life Support Systems Training and Acquisition Manager 001687
Job Family                                  NOC                 Short Title (30 Characters)                       Short Title (14 Characters)
Management                                  TBD                 ALSS TRAINING ACQUISITION MGR                     ALSS TRACQ MGR
Pay Plan              Career Field          Other Relationships and Rules
Enlisted              PR                    NEC 788A
Job Description
Aviation Life Support Systems Training and Acquisition Managers perform critical acquisition-type and training activities and functions (i.e., Integrated
Logistics Support (ILS), Naval Air Training Management Support Activity (NATMSACT)); are responsible for acquisition systems development and
testing, and logistic support for acquisition programs oversight, review, and acceptance of supplies and services; ensure reliability and maintainability for
systems design, the development of acquisition and logistics plans and documents, system integration, logistics support analysis, provisioning,
configuration, management, systems modifications, and site activation or program planning, oversight, and acceptance of supplies and services; are
responsible for various requirements related to the development and execution of budgets, acquisition and logistics support of programs.

Aircrew Survival Equipmentmen (PR) inspect, maintain, test, troubleshoot, repair, and manage Aviation Life Support Systems (ALSS) programs, oxygen systems, parachutes, seat pans, survival equipment, electronic and physical records, and flight and protective clothing and equipment; pack and rig parachutes; pack and equip flotation equipment; fit and maintain oxygen masks, flight clothing, anti-exposure suits, and anti-gravity suits; operate and maintain Carbon Dioxide (CO2) transfer and recharge equipment; operate and repair sewing machines; conduct special calendar/periodic inspections of survival equipment; pack and perform Quality Assurance Inspections (QAI) on static line and military freefall parachutes; conduct Jumpmaster Personnel Inspections (JMPIs); perform duties as Drop Zone Safety Officer and Malfunction Officer in support of Premeditated Personnel Parachuting (P3) operations; and supervise operation of parachute lofts and survival equipment work centers. __________________________________________

Aviation Life Support Systems Training and Acquisition Managers perform critical acquisition-type and training activities and functions (i.e., Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), Naval Air Training Management Support Activity (NATMSACT)); are responsible for acquisition systems development and testing, and logistic support for acquisition programs oversight, review, and acceptance of supplies and services; ensure reliability and maintainability for systems design, the development of acquisition and logistics plans and documents, system integration, logistics support analysis, provisioning, configuration, management, systems modifications, and site activation or program planning, oversight, and acceptance of supplies and services; are responsible for various requirements related to the development and execution of budgets, acquisition and logistics support of programs.

Coordinate Fleet Air Introduction Liaison Survival Aircrew Flight Equipment (FAILSAFE) programs.
Manage Aviation Life Support System (ALSS) fleet support programs (e.g., Program Manager Air (PMA), Fleet Support Team (FST), Class Desk, etc.).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
